chunks: With this chain of transmission, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a menstruating woman who sees purity: may her husband have intercourse with her before she performs ghusl (ritual bath)? He said: “There is no harm, though after ghusl (ritual bath) is more beloved to me.”

Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, said: As for the mustahadah, she is the one who sees, outside the days of her menses, thin, cold, clear blood. What contains the description of the blood of istihadah has already preceded at the beginning of the chapter. Then he said: She must wash her private part from it, then insert cotton, and bind the place with cloths so that the cotton is prevented from coming out. If the blood is slight and does not soak through onto the cloths, nor appear on them due to its small amount, then she must remove the cotton at the time of every salat (prayer), perform istinja', change the cotton and cloths, and renew wudu (ablution) for the salat (prayer). If the blood has seeped onto the cloths slightly but has not flowed from them, then she must change the cotton and cloths at salat (prayer) al-fajr after istinja' with water, then perform wudu (ablution) for the salat (prayer), and perform ghusl (ritual bath) after wudu (ablution) for this salat (prayer), and renew wudu (ablution) and change the cotton and cloths at every salat (prayer) without ghusl (ritual bath). If the blood is abundant so that it seeps onto the cloths and flows from them, then it is obligatory upon her to delay salat (prayer) al-zuhr from the beginning of its time, then remove the cloths and cotton, cleanse herself with water, resume with clean cotton and pure cloths with which she binds herself tightly, perform the wudu (ablution) of salat (prayer), then perform ghusl (ritual bath), and pray with that ghusl (ritual bath) and wudu (ablution) salat (prayer) al-zuhr and al-'asr together in combination. She should do the like of that for al-maghrib and 'isha' al-akhirah, delaying al-maghrib from the beginning of its time so that her completion of it is at the disappearance of the twilight, and bringing forward 'isha' al-akhirah at the beginning of its time. She should do the like of that for salat (prayer) al-layl and al-ghadah; if she leaves salat (prayer) al-layl, she does that for salat (prayer) al-ghadah. If she performs wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath) according to what we have described, it is lawful for her husband to have intercourse with her, and that is not permissible for him until she does what we have mentioned of removing the cloths and washing the private part with water. The mustahadah does not leave sawm (fasting) and salat (prayer) during her state of istihadah; rather, she leaves them in the days in which she used to habitually menstruate before her condition changed to istihadah. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: cessation of menstruation and return to ritual purity from menses
key_terms.الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ: irregular uterine bleeding outside the days of menstruation
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ritual bath required in specified states of ritual impurity
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةُ: a woman experiencing irregular non-menstrual bleeding

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for intercourse, ghusl (ritual bath), wudu (ablution), and salat (prayer) for a menstruating woman after purity and for a mustahadah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses legal rulings concerning a woman who has become pure from menstruation and the rulings of istihadah. It explains when intercourse is permissible, and details the required measures of purification, wudu (ablution), ghusl (ritual bath), and salat (prayer) according to the amount of blood seen. It also states that the mustahadah continues salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting), except during the days of her established menstrual habit.
